get.description:
Catalog discovery is a non-metered local read. It filters enabled routes by your key model allowlist, current group permissions and channel or plugin bindings. It does not call an upstream, reserve quota or update inference usage. Enabled or exhausted keys can read with zero balance; expired, disabled and invalid keys are rejected.

Catalog prices are customer unit rates for this key, represented as decimal strings in currency. Missing fields are not free prices; an explicit "0" is a configured zero price. Different eligible routes or groups, request options and unsupported complex expressions can produce variable=true instead of an inaccurate flat price. Unknown model capabilities are omitted.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional for task-backed submissions; required by DFLOP and asynchronous speech contracts. Use 1–200 printable ASCII characters without surrounding whitespace; do not put secrets here. Scope: authenticated API key, method and concrete operation path. Same key and equivalent JSON/multipart payload replay the same retained, owned task without another submission or charge. Changed payload returns 409 idempotency_key_conflict; concurrent/uncertain attempts return 409 idempotency_in_progress/idempotency_indeterminate. Discarded immediate results return idempotency_replay_unavailable without resubmitting. Minimum retention is 72 hours and 48 hours after task completion; active/uncertain records are not automatically removed. A funding attempt that cannot be reconciled keeps the key blocked for operator recovery; do not bypass it with a new key. Normal authentication and allowance still apply. Only the task submission pipeline supports this guarantee; synchronous relay fallback and WebSocket do not. JSON is limited to 16 MiB, depth 32 and 65536 nodes; multipart to 128 MiB, 128 parts and 1 MiB per field. See /docs/developer-idempotency.

get.description:
Only tasks created by this API key are visible; another key of the same user has no access. Availability depends on retained records. These local reads are non-metered and private no-store; zero allowance is readable, but disabled, expired or IP-restricted credentials are rejected.

On this GET route, {key} is the public task ID; on POST it is the plugin key. Task status uses the existing video status vocabulary. Timestamps are Unix seconds; optional timestamps and request_id are omitted when unavailable. A failed task exposes a generic error, not the provider failure payload.

get.summary: Read recorded usage for the current API key
get.description:
Only records created by this API key are included; another key of the same user has no access. Availability depends on retained records. Amounts are decimal strings in the configured display unit, not wallet balances or complete final charges. This local read is non-metered and private no-store; zero allowance is readable.

Optional start and end are Unix seconds for [start, end); the default is the last 30 days and the maximum window is 31 days. Optional model filters the recorded model. billing_events and error_events count recorded events, not requests or successes. Components use proven frozen billing units; component_status is available, partial or unknown. Unknown usage is not converted into synthetic media tokens. Refunds recorded in this interval can relate to consumption outside it, so recorded_net may be negative. Task components show the latest proven snapshot per task within the window, not an incremental request-count or unit ledger.
